message.reasoning:
I am reviewing the Monopoly game state to prepare a decision.

I have $2966 and three hotels on my properties. The opponent has almost no cash and owns several heavily mortgaged properties with mostly four houses or one hotel. I am weighing whether to trade, unmortgage, or sell buildings.

I will not unmortgage the railroad or Tennessee Avenue. I will not trade cash or get-out-of-jail cards for Tennessee Avenue. I will not sell my hotels. My cash covers the rent on Park Place and Boardwalk.

I am on New York Avenue and will roll next. I see no benefit in trading with the opponent, who has almost no cash.

Tennessee Avenue is mortgaged for $90. Unmortgaging it would cost $99. The opponent already owns the other orange properties, so I would not collect rent from it. Pennsylvania Railroad is mortgaged for $100 and would cost $110 to unmortgage.

I would collect only $25 rent from one unmortgaged railroad, so that is not worthwhile. Selling my hotels would destroy my kill power, and I should not trade cash for their income-generating properties.

I am calculating the rent on my pink hotels. St. Charles Place and States Avenue each pay $750 with a hotel, while Virginia Avenue pays $900. The opponent has only $34 cash, so landing on any pink would bankrupt them unless they liquidate their buildings first. Selling houses costs half the build price.

Light blue houses sell for $25 each. Dark blue houses sell for $100 each. A hotel sells back for half its cost, which equals five houses. The Connecticut hotel would return $125 if sold.

I will end my turn. I am now calculating which spaces I might land on from New York Avenue.

From New York Avenue, the next roll can only land on Free Parking, Kentucky, Chance, Indiana, Illinois, B&O, Atlantic, Ventnor, Water Works, Marvin Gardens, or Go to Jail. Park Place and Boardwalk are unreachable in one turn.

Jail is safe from their dark blue properties. Most reachable spaces are mortgaged, so I am secure from rent this turn. I will pass and keep the message short.
